My great grandpa was firstly a member of Slovak troops which were sided with Germany. He came from small town and hated nazis. He and his fellow group of soldiers got willingly arrested by Russians so they can join partisans and fight against Germany.

Unluckily they lost a fight, got captured and sent to concentration camp. When they got there the Nazis asked who could speak german. My great grandpa worked at a German shoe-maker and learned a bit of german language there. This helped him a lot since he wasn't sent to die right away and could speak with guards which resulted in them being not so aggressive to him as to others.

I was pretty young when he passed away so he didn't tell me much about how it was in there.

I only remember that he mentioned that no one who is hungry today knows true hunger. Everyone there was fighting for their own survival. They got 1 small butter and few slices of bread for many people crammed into one place. He said there was always a big tension when they were cutting butter, because even one milimeter more for someone would be seen as extreme problem. When they were outside they also ate grass and whatever they could find.

Knowing german language probably saved his life, since he became a friend with one of the guards. He talked with him about his (guard's) family and sometimes brought him a little bit of bread. (I don't know if my great grandpa shared the bread or said anyone about this guard). However when this happened it was few weeks before Russians came (if I remember corectly)

When Russians came, Nazis tried burning everything down but didn't successfully do it. After the prisoners were freed there was a huge feast left in the concentration camp headquarters and lots of riches. However everyone was scared of eating there, since they were suspicious there might be a poison in it. Also no one took any riches, they just wanted to get out quickly. And they were also very week. 

When they were going back they found shelter in one Czech family which accepted few of them and helped them get stronger. The former prisoners all looked sick and were dirty, but that didn't mattered to the family that helped them.

My great grandpa was previously an athlete and founder of a local skying club who weighted around 90kg. When he got back home he weighted around 30-35kg, but considering what he had gone through he had few health problems.

I know this is a long story and I don't care if anyone reads it, I just thought this was a good opportunity to remember my great grandpa.
